To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Maternal depression is common, and is associated with a range of adverse child and family outcomes.

1) the prevalence of depression among mothers is high, and is especially high among unmarried mothers; 2) depression is a chronic condition among many mothers, with about 38% of mothers reporting depression at least once over the course of the study; and 3) employment and relationship status are among the most robust predictors of maternal depression.
